newsitem.title: UK: Mediterranean oil products firmer with crude.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean oil products firmer with crude.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were broadly firmer on Thursday, traders said.
Gasoline was slightly firmer alongside futures although traders said transatlantic arbitrage options were more limited as European prices matched the gains of the U.S. markets.
Poor reforming margins continue to cap refinery output of high octane grades, while low octane supplies continue to grow. But high octane grades were not in great demand.
Naphtha edged up with crude. Offers for prompt cargoes were scarce, but this was countered by more relaxed buying interest.
The 60kt Algerian cargo in the market since last Friday was still talked at around cif high quotes +$2/+3 but the holder, Petrobras, is expected to take the cargo transatlantic.
Gas oil was firm, but heavy supplies of Russian cargoes put pressure on premiums. Four distressed Russian parcels on the water on Wednesday sold at just cif quotes high evens and +$1.
"Underlying prices are good, but the premiums for Russian cargoes have gone from +$3 to +50 cents in a matter of days,"a trader said.
High sulphur cracked fuel oil was firmer and still tight, traders said.
An Italian cargo was heard sold to a trader at a $1 over the quoted fob high, but this was not confirmed and some dealers thought the number a little low.
Two bunker requirements were seen for Tunisia though a northern Spanish cargo may have moved to cover one of those.

A mid-month Egyptian straight-run cargo was available, and offers were talked close to $10 over the quoted high cif. But buyers were expected to be as much as $5 under those levels, given the better supply of Russian material in the region.
A-960 cargoes may become available in the Med although prices east of the Gulf were thought slightly more attractive.
